note: What each guard CANNOT catch. Every bug on 2026-08-23 was a check that was right in principle and asked a question whose answer could not reveal the fault — not a broken guard, a guard aimed slightly beside the thing it guards. We declare blind spots for every agent and declared none for guards, so a guard asking the wrong question looked identical to one that works.
law: Writing the sentence IS the work. Anybody made to write 'measures elapsed time, not whether a scheduled run happened' would have seen the gap before it cost a morning. A blind spot too vague to reveal a gap is not a blind spot.

schema-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: Values. A file with every key present and an index of 8,123,456 passes every structural test ever written — shape checking cannot see whether a number is absurd.

flag-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: A gate that is registered, owned, documented and simply wrong. It verifies each flag exists once with an owner and a trigger; it has no view on whether the trigger is the right trigger.

memory-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether a law is CORRECT. It checks the knowledge base is current, readable and cross-referenced. A wrong law, perfectly formatted and reachable from the entry point, passes cleanly.
memory-guard.mjs.coveredBy: the falsifier, and being wrong in public

competence-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether a declared principle is TRUE. It enforces that every specialist declares sourced principles, failure modes, blind spots and a recheck date. A confidently wrong principle with a real citation passes.
competence-guard.mjs.coveredBy: the teacher, and the recheck date

knowledge-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether a source is any good. It requires every fact to carry sources, a date and a falsifier. Three secondary sources agreeing with each other satisfied it — and our own catalogue disproved the number.
knowledge-guard.mjs.coveredBy: verify-work's secondary-consensus check, added after exactly that

content-sanity.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether prose is GOOD. It catches labels in prose slots, unresolved templates, truncation and copy too short to be an explanation. A fluent, well-formed, entirely wrong sentence passes.

layout-check.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether a design looks GOOD. It measures clipping, overlap and empty panels against real font metrics. Geometry is not taste and a balanced, ugly page passes.

card-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the IMAGE is right. It reads the SVG source, so a card back served as a 200 PNG at correct dimensions passed everything — the bytes were valid and the picture was of the wrong thing.
card-guard.mjs.coveredBy: reading image URLs from source data rather than constructing them, and eyes

slop-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: A grouping that IS in the data and still means nothing. It enforces that every grouping derives from a held field or an openly stored list; a technically-derived and utterly boring grouping passes.

verify-work.mjs.cannotCatch: Reasoning. It checks whether output carries what a defensible claim must carry. The pooled-cohort error that nearly retired a correct thesis would have passed it cleanly.
verify-work.mjs.coveredBy: the decision log, which grades predictions rather than logic

bias-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: Its own bias. It was written by the same party it audits, and its measure of whether the machines are calibrated is a count the machines produce.
bias-guard.mjs.coveredBy: Tyler catching what the machines miss — the ratio IS the score

publish-assert.mjs.cannotCatch: Anything published through a path it does not read. Hand-minted cards went straight to Tyler twice, once with a wrong price and once meaningless, and this never saw either.
publish-assert.mjs.coveredBy: verify-work's ungated-publication check, added after exactly that

windowless-price-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: A figure with a window that is WRONG. It requires a date range; it cannot tell whether the range is accurate or whether the provider is describing it honestly.
windowless-price-guard.mjs.coveredBy: the graded-window probe, which measures rather than asks

domain-plausibility.mjs.cannotCatch: An implausible value that is nevertheless true. Its rules encode what we believe about the hobby, so a genuine market shock reads as a filter fault — it names our own filter as first suspect, which is right almost always and wrong sometimes.

guard-audit.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether a wired guard asks the right question. It verifies guards exist, are connected and run in order. The heartbeat was wired, ordered, running — and green through a failed run.

heartbeat.mjs.cannotCatch: A run that fires, succeeds, and produces wrong data. It now detects missed scheduled runs; it has no view on whether a completed run did anything useful.
knownPatterns: elapsed time as a proxy for an event
heartbeat.mjs.history: Allowed 30 hours so a LATE run would not cry wolf, which is exactly the window a SKIPPED run hides in. Reported green through a failed fetch on 2026-08-23.

qa-gate.mjs.cannotCatch: A number that is fresh, thick and wrong. It checks sample size, staleness and coverage — 26 listings kept from 150 fetched cleared every threshold while our own filter had eaten the market.

voice-lint.mjs.cannotCatch: Copy that is on-voice and says nothing. It catches hype, hedging and forbidden phrasing. The word 'chase' published as an entire explanation passed it — perfectly on-voice, perfectly meaningless.

jargon-lint.mjs.cannotCatch: A term we have taught badly. It flags unexplained jargon; it cannot tell whether the explanation given is any good, and 'the 9 rarely pays — only the 10' had a tooltip nobody could parse.

falsifier.mjs.cannotCatch: A thesis it is testing WRONGLY. It reported RT-5 TRIPPED because it pooled two cohorts the thesis explicitly contrasts — the thesis was 11 of 12 accurate and the test was measuring the average of a contrast. It matches card names when splitting RT-5 cohorts, which is the substring shape — mitigated by word boundaries and a hand-checked twelve-card set, and worth revisiting the moment that set grows.
falsifier.mjs.coveredBy: the contrastive-thesis guard in negative-tests, added after exactly that

correction-hunter.mjs.cannotCatch: A figure that never moves. It re-checks published numbers that changed; a price frozen for a month is a claim too, and it is invisible here.
correction-hunter.mjs.coveredBy: the teacher raised exactly this question

rasterize-cards.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the rendered image is CORRECT. It confirms a PNG was produced at the right size. A card back renders identically to a card front.
rasterize-cards.mjs.coveredBy: reading image URLs from source, and eyes

build-corrections.mjs.cannotCatch: NOT A GUARD. It generates the public corrections page. Listed in the audit because the audit tracks pipeline steps as well as checks, and conflating the two is how a generator gets read as a safety net. It also writes font stacks in the shorthand form, which is the shape that let four pages render headings in Times — acknowledged and fixed, kept on the record because the shape recurs.

pre-mortem.mjs.cannotCatch: A shape it has never been bitten by. Every pattern here was added AFTER something shipped, so the table is a record of our history, not a model of risk — it is structurally blind to the next novel failure and will stay so until that one costs a morning too. It also matches on SOURCE TEXT, so a guard that carries a shape inside a string or a comment reads as carrying the shape, and one that expresses the same fault through a helper or a computed value reads as clean.
pre-mortem.mjs.coveredBy: Nothing automatic. New shapes arrive only from a real failure being written up — which is why the report matters more than the scan.

editor-smoke.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the page LOOKS right, and whether the images actually resolve. It runs the emitted script against a minimal DOM and confirms cards and themes render — it has no browser, no layout, no network, so a page that loads perfectly and shows 24 card backs passes cleanly.
editor-smoke.mjs.coveredBy: CC with screenshots, and the constructed-URL fallback
editor-smoke.mjs.history: Written after the editor shipped three times in two days rendering nothing — verified to PARSE each time, never verified to WORK.

tease-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: A tease that withholds perfectly and is boring. It checks that nothing names the product; it has no view on whether the mystery is INTERESTING, and 'it arrives in a box' withholds everything and might intrigue nobody.
tease-guard.mjs.coveredBy: Tyler, and whether anybody replies asking what it is
tease-guard.mjs.history: Written after 'Catch'em Guards ???' shipped — the name answered the question the tag was pretending to withhold, and 'not a toploader, not a binder' then named the category while sounding like a denial. Nobody was checking.

creators-smoke.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the pairings are any GOOD. It confirms the page loads, renders pairings and images, and that every inline handler is reachable. It has no view on whether a pairing is worth posting.
creators-smoke.mjs.history: Written after every button on the portal was found dead — grab, setup, pick and toX all declared, none on window, and a top-level await inside a non-async grab() meant the whole script never ran. It parsed perfectly the entire time.

live-smoke.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the slides are worth talking about. It proves the two views stay synced, that the presenter always sees a confidence tier, and that no unverified claim reaches the overlay as stated fact. It has no view on whether a prompt would actually start a good segment.
live-smoke.mjs.coveredBy: Tyler using it live, and the post-outcome log
live-smoke.mjs.history: Found two real bugs on its first run: BroadcastChannel does not replay, so the audience opened blank whenever it started after the presenter, which is the normal order; and the audience posted its hello BEFORE assigning onmessage, so it could not hear the answer.

offline-smoke.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the images actually RESOLVE. It proves the page renders its catalogue with no network at all and that the srcs are well-formed. A page rendering 36 broken-image icons would pass.
offline-smoke.mjs.coveredBy: CC with a real browser, and Tyler opening it
offline-smoke.mjs.history: Written after I certified the editor as working using a harness that supplied a FAKE FETCH which always succeeded. Opened from file://, Chrome blocks fetch of a sibling file, INDEX stayed empty, and no images, no themes and no search results all followed from that single cause.

theme-smoke.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether a theme's output is INTERESTING. It proves every theme produces something at its own declared counts and that no two return identical card sets. A theme producing six dull pairings passes cleanly.
theme-smoke.mjs.coveredBy: the post-outcome log, and Tyler clicking through
theme-smoke.mjs.history: Written after Tyler found that only the artist themes worked, two returned identical results, and the rest produced nothing. Cause: buildIdeas switched on theme ID, so a theme without a branch failed silently, and artist-career and first-and-last shared one. It then found three more faults immediately, including a bestAt of 'late evening' where card counts belonged, and two themes that were the same theme written twice.

editor-hostile.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the abuse it survives is the abuse a real person commits. It tries what I could think of, which is not the same as what somebody will do.
editor-hostile.mjs.coveredBy: Tyler using it, and CC with a browser

editor-copy-rules.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the copy is GOOD. It proves nothing asserts, names a grade or leaks a JS value. A dull line that breaks no rule passes.
editor-copy-rules.mjs.coveredBy: Tyler using it, and CC with a browser

editor-claim-match.mjs.cannotCatch: A claim that is wrong about something OUTSIDE the cards. It checks counts, duplicates, named artists and card existence — not whether the underlying fact is true.
editor-claim-match.mjs.coveredBy: Tyler using it, and CC with a browser

editor-money-credit.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the prices are ACCURATE. It checks for absurd values and for the unpriced count being shown, not for a price being right.
editor-money-credit.mjs.coveredBy: Tyler using it, and CC with a browser

rating-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the derivation is a GOOD one. It proves every rating names a printed field and that refused ratings stay refused. It has no view on whether 'an unevolved Basic at 60 HP' is actually a fair proxy for cute — that is a judgement, and only Tyler and the outcome log can settle it.
rating-guard.mjs.coveredBy: Tyler, and whether the filters find what people expect
rating-guard.mjs.history: Written alongside the bios. Tyler asked for cuteness, comedy and popularity ratings; the honest version derives each from a printed field and the dishonest version is me assigning scores that feel right. Popularity and likeness were REFUSED outright for having no signal, and this guard exists so they cannot quietly reappear.

crop-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: Where X ACTUALLY crops. 1.25 is our best understanding of the timeline crop and it is not documented by X — if the real number is lower, every layout passes this guard and still clips. The margin is protection against rounding, not against a wrong constant.
crop-guard.mjs.coveredBy: Tyler, who is the only person who can see a real timeline
crop-guard.mjs.history: Written after the 2x2 clipped at the top. I had targeted EXACTLY 1.25 — the crop line itself — so there was zero tolerance for rounding or device pixel ratio. Designing to a limit means failing at the limit.

ask-smoke.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the cards it returns are the RIGHT ones. It proves every prompt fills the tray; it has no view on whether "something dark" returned anything actually dark.
ask-smoke.mjs.history: Written after seven of eleven prompts left the tray empty. The box promised a post and handed back a filtered grid, and the cause was thirteen word-boundary escapes emitting as BACKSPACE characters so every match silently failed.

evo-smoke.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the CARD chosen at each stage is the nicest one available. It proves the line is the right line and the right length; it has no view on whether a nicer Charmeleon existed.
evo-smoke.mjs.history: Written after "charizard evolution from 151" announced Charizard and returned Chansey and Blissey. Sixteen named lines are now checked on every build.
